mainTopic: From the עץ הדעת and בת שבע's rebuke of שלמה to the meals that do not make a בן סורר ומורה liable
overview: This amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת about which plant the עץ הדעת was: a grapevine, wheat, or a fig, with a reason for each view. It then explains a פסוק in משלי as בת שבע rebuking her son שלמה for drinking too much, phrase by phrase. רבי יצחק shows from another פסוק that שלמה later admitted she was right. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה about the בן סורר ומורה and works through its list of meals that do not make the son liable. These are eating with a מצוה group, at the עיבור החודש gathering, eating מעשר שני in ירושלים, eating forbidden meats, and eating tied to a מצוה or an עבירה. Along the way, רבי אבהו says liability needs a group made up entirely of idlers, and רבא says bird meat alone does not count. A פסוק teaches that the law is about disobeying parents, not God. The amud ends by explaining that 'any food' and 'any drink' include pressed figs, honey and milk, and starts a ברייתא about a כהן who ate them, whose ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine brings wailing: the reason for the grapevine view
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the reasoning of the view (רבי מאיר's, from just before this section) that the עץ הדעת was a grapevine: nothing brings a person grief like wine does.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there is nothing that brings wailing to a person except wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the reason for the first opinion, that the עץ הדעת was a grapevine. The proof is that wine, more than anything else, still brings trouble and crying to people today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the fruit that brought the first sin and its sorrow into the world should be the same kind of thing that still brings sorrow today. Wine fits that description best, so the tree must have been a grapevine.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tree of Knowledge in גן עדן, the subject of this מחלוקת
Wailing or crying, meaning trouble and grief

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the עץ הדעת back to the larger theme of the סוגיא: the dangers of wine.

phrases.english: for there is no thing
that brings wailing to a person
except wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁמֵּבִיא יְלָלָה לְאָדָם אֶלָּא יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the grapevine opinion begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עץ הדעת was a grapevine, because wine is what brings wailing to people.

steps.title: The tree was wheat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the עץ הדעת was wheat, because a baby only starts to 'know' to call Abba and Imma after tasting grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It was wheat, because a baby does not know how to call 'Abba' and 'Imma' until he tastes the taste of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second opinion: the עץ הדעת was wheat. His proof is that grain is linked to a child's first real knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree is called the tree of 'knowledge', so רבי יהודה looks for a food that brings knowledge. He points out that a baby begins to recognize and name his parents only once he eats grain, so grain is the food of knowledge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It was wheat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַתִּינוֹק יוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹא אַבָּא וְאִימָּא
phrases.english: for a baby does not know how to call 'Father' and 'Mother'
until he tastes the taste of grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, competing identification of the עץ הדעת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עץ הדעת was wheat, since grain is linked to the start of knowledge.

steps.title: The tree was a fig
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the עץ הדעת was a fig tree, because אדם and חוה fixed their situation with fig leaves, the same thing they sinned with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: It was a fig, for they were repaired with the very thing they ruined themselves with, as it says: 'And they sewed fig leaves.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives a third opinion: the עץ הדעת was a fig tree. He proves it from the פסוק that אדם and חוה covered themselves with fig leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is that the repair comes from the same source as the damage. Right after they sinned, they covered themselves with fig leaves, so the tree they sinned with was most likely a fig tree too.

keyTerms.meaning: They spoiled or ruined, meaning they sinned

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the עץ הדעת: grapevine (wine brings grief), wheat (grain brings knowledge), and fig (they were repaired with fig leaves).

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: It was a fig,
for with the thing they ruined themselves with, they were repaired,
as it says: 'And they sewed fig leaves.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third identification, this time backed by a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עץ הדעת was a fig tree, since they were repaired with fig leaves.

steps.title: בת שבע ties her son to a pillar
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'the words of King למואל... with which his mother corrected him', רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that his mother tied him to a pillar and rebuked him with three phrases.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The words of King למואל, the burden with which his mother corrected him.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: This teaches that his mother tied him to a pillar and said to him: 'What, my son? And what, son of my womb? And what, son of my vows?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about wine. It explains that the 'correction' in the פסוק was a real punishment, with a three-part rebuke. This step sets up the next three steps, which explain each part of that rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יסרתו' (corrected him) is read as actual discipline: she bound him to a pillar. Her words come from the next פסוק, and each phrase will be explained separately in the coming steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A name used for King שלמה in this פסוק
She tied him up or forced him

phrases.english: 'The words of Lemuel, the king,'
phrases.notes: משלי 31:1. The גמרא reads למואל as שלמה, and his mother as בת שבע.

phrases.english: 'the burden with which his mother corrected him.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
This teaches that his mother tied him to the pillar

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה לוֹ, ״מַה בְּרִי וּמַה בַּר בִּטְנִי
phrases.english: and said to him: 'What, my son? And what, son of my womb?'
'And what, son of my vows?'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכְּפָאַתּוּ אִמּוֹ עַל הָעַמּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עץ הדעת to a new אגדה teaching on the dangers of wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'correction' in the פסוק was שלמה's mother binding him to a pillar and rebuking him in three phrases.

steps.title: 'My son': people will blame your mother
steps.stepSummary: The first phrase means: everyone knows your father was God-fearing, so if you go wrong they will blame me, your mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'What, my son?' Everyone knows your father was God-fearing. Now they will say his mother caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first part of the rebuke, 'מה ברי'. בת שבע tells שלמה that his bad behavior will be blamed on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since דוד's fear of Heaven was well known, people would not blame the father. The blame would land on the mother, so she stresses that he is 'her' son.

phrases.english: 'What, my son?' Everyone knows
that your father was God-fearing,
now they will say: his mother caused it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מַה בְּרִי״ – הַכֹּל יוֹדְעִים שֶׁאָבִיךְ יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three phrases quoted in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'My son' means: your sin will be blamed on your mother.

steps.title: 'Son of my womb': I worked to give you strength
steps.stepSummary: The second phrase means: the other wives stopped going to the king once they were pregnant, but I went in anyway so my son would be strong and fair.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And what, son of my womb?' All the women of your father's house, once they became pregnant, no longer saw the king's face. But I pushed my way in, so that I would have a son who is strong and fair-skinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second phrase, 'בר בטני'. בת שבע reminds שלמה of the extra effort she made during her pregnancy for his benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She went to the king while pregnant, which the other wives did not do, so that her child would be strong and good-looking. Her point is that he is now wasting those gifts on drinking.

phrases.aramaic: ״וּמַה בַּר בִּטְנִי״ – כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ,
phrases.english: 'And what, son of my womb?' All the women of your father's house,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁמִּתְעַבְּרוֹת, שׁוּב אֵינָן רוֹאוֹת פְּנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
phrases.english: once they became pregnant, would no longer see the face of the king.
But I pushed and went in,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא לִי בֵּן מְזוֹרָז וּמְלוּבָּן.
phrases.english: so that I would have a son who is strong and fair-skinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּמַה בַּר בִּטְנִי״ – כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second of the three phrases quoted in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Son of my womb' means: I went out of my way during pregnancy so you would be strong and fair.

steps.title: 'Son of my vows': I prayed for a son of תורה and prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The third phrase means: the other wives vowed for a son fit to be king, but I vowed for a son who is diligent, full of תורה, and fit for prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And what, son of my vows?' All the women of your father's house used to vow: 'Let me have a son fit for kingship.' But I vowed and said: 'Let me have a son who is diligent, filled with תורה, and fit for prophecy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third and last phrase, 'בר נדרי'. בת שבע tells שלמה that she hoped and vowed for much more than a king: she wanted a son of תורה and prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast is between the other wives' goal of a royal son and her higher goal of a spiritual son. Drinking too much betrays the very hopes she vowed for him.
steps.whatToRemember: בת שבע's three-part rebuke: 'my son' (people will blame me), 'son of my womb' (I worked to make you strong), 'son of my vows' (I vowed for a son of תורה and prophecy). All of it was aimed at stopping שלמה from drinking.

phrases.aramaic: ״וּמָה בַּר נְדָרָי״ – כָּל נָשִׁים שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ
phrases.english: 'And what, son of my vows?' All the women of your father's house

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ נוֹדְרוֹת: ״יְהֵא לִי בֵּן הָגוּן לַמַּלְכוּת״,
phrases.english: used to vow: 'Let me have a son fit for kingship,'

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי נָדַרְתִּי וְאָמַרְתִּי: ״יְהֵא לִי בֵּן זָרִיז
phrases.english: but I vowed and said: 'Let me have a son who is diligent'
'and filled with Torah, and fit for prophecy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּמָה בַּר נְדָרָי״ – כָּל נָשִׁים שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ הָיוּ נוֹדְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third of the three phrases quoted in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Son of my vows' means: I vowed for a son full of תורה and fit for prophecy, not just a king.

steps.title: Kings should not drink and forget God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the next פסוק of בת שבע's rebuke: a king like שלמה should not drink wine like other kings who get drunk and push God away.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is not for kings, למואל, it is not for kings to drink wine.' She told him: why be like kings who get drunk and say 'Why do we need God?' 'Nor for princes, where is strong drink': should someone who knows all the world's secrets drink and get drunk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading בת שבע's words to שלמה. It explains two parts of the פסוק as warnings against drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אל למלכים' are read as a play on words: kings who say 'למה לנו אל', 'why do we need God'. The word 'רוזנים' (princes) is read like 'רזי' (secrets). Someone who holds the world's secrets should not dull his mind with wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for שלמה used in this פסוק

phrases.english: "It is not for kings, O Lemoel,
it is not for kings to drink wine."
"It is not for kings": she said to him:
What do you have to do with kings
who drink wine and get drunk
and say, "Why do we need God?"
phrases.notes: A play on words: 'אל למלכים' is heard as 'למה לנו אל', 'why do we need God'.

phrases.english: "Nor for princes, where is strong drink":

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁכׇּל רָזֵי עוֹלָם גְּלוּיִים לוֹ
phrases.english: should one to whom all the secrets of the world are revealed
drink wine and get drunk?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל לַמְלָכִים לְמוֹאֵל, אַל לַמְלָכִים שְׁתוֹ יָיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining בת שבע's rebuke of שלמה, moving to the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king, and especially one who holds the world's secrets, should not drink wine and get drunk like kings who reject God.

steps.title: Another reading: princes come to his door
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion reads 'רוזנים' simply as princes: all the world's rulers come to שלמה's door, so he should not get drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: should someone whose door all the princes of the world come to early in the morning drink wine and get drunk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to read the word 'רוזנים' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading made 'רוזנים' into 'secrets'. This reading keeps its plain meaning, 'princes'. The point is the same: a man with so much honor and responsibility should not get drunk.

phrases.english: Some say:
should one for whom all the princes of the world
come early to his door
drink wine and get drunk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of 'ולרוזנים' from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'רוזנים' means the princes who come to שלמה's door, so he must not get drunk.

steps.title: שלמה admitted his mother was right
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק asks how we know שלמה later admitted his mother was right, and brings a פסוק where שלמה calls himself foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: How do we know שלמה came back and admitted to his mother? As it says: 'For I am more foolish than a man, and I do not have the understanding of a person.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק wants to show that שלמה accepted his mother's rebuke, and brings a פסוק as proof. The next step explains how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story so far was about the mother's rebuke. רבי יצחק adds the ending: שלמה admitted he had acted foolishly. The proof is a פסוק in משלי where he speaks about his own foolishness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that Shlomo came back
and admitted to his mother?
As it is written: "For I am more foolish than a man,
and I do not have the understanding of a person."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the rebuke by showing שלמה's response.
steps.raayaObject: That שלמה admitted his mother's rebuke was right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 30:2, 'כי בער אנכי מאיש ולא בינת אדם לי'.

steps.title: More foolish than נח and אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is explained: 'איש' means נח and 'אדם' means אדם הראשון, so שלמה admits he was as foolish as them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'More foolish than a man' means more than נח, who is called 'a man of the earth'. 'Not the understanding of a person' means אדם הראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decodes the two words of the פסוק, 'איש' and 'אדם', as two famous people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח is linked through the word 'איש' in 'איש האדמה'. Both נח and אדם הראשון are connected to wine: נח got drunk, and according to the view earlier on this דף (step 1), the עץ הדעת was a grapevine. So שלמה is admitting that his drinking was a real mistake, just as his mother warned.

keyTerms.meaning: Man of the earth, a title for נח

steps.whatToRemember: בת שבע rebuked שלמה about wine, and he later admitted she was right, comparing himself to נח and אדם הראשון.

phrases.english: "For I am more foolish than a man": than Noach,
as it is written: "And Noach, the man of the earth, began."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:20. The shared word 'איש' is what links this פסוק to נח.

phrases.english: "And I do not have the understanding of a person":
this is Adam, the first man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 10 proves שלמה admitted his mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'איש' is נח and 'אדם' is אדם הראשון; שלמה admits he was more foolish than both.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: eating with a מצוה group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a son who ate with a group gathered for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: he ate with a group gathered for a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story section is over, and the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה. This line sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a son who ate his meat and wine at a מצוה gathering does not become a בן סורר ומורה. The גמרא quotes this line so it can now discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: A group gathered to do a מצוה

phrases.english: He ate with a group gathered for a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son who eats with a group gathered for a מצוה is not a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Liable only with a group of idlers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the son is only liable if he ate with a group made up entirely of idlers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: he is not liable unless he eats with a group that is all idlers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a new condition: the bad meal only counts if all the people he ate with were idlers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the danger of a בן סורר ומורה is being pulled into a bad crowd. If even some decent people are at the table, the meal does not make him liable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
He is not liable unless he eats
with a group that is made up entirely of idlers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל בַּחֲבוּרָה שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ סְרִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition for liability connected to the משנה's line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן סורר ומורה is liable only if he ate with a group made up entirely of idlers.

steps.title: Doesn't the משנה suggest otherwise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו: the משנה implies that only a מצוה group protects him, so any other group, even one not all idlers, would make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: if he ate with a מצוה group, he is not a בן סורר ומורה. The reason is the מצוה. So if it was not a מצוה, he would be liable even if the group was not all idlers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and finds what looks like a contradiction to רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives only one reason for exemption: the מצוה. That suggests any non-מצוה meal makes him liable, even with decent people present. That clashes with רבי אבהו, who says he is liable only with a group that is all idlers.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the Mishnah:
If he ate with a group gathered for a מצוה,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.
The reason is that it was a מצוה.
So if it was not a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו כּוּלָּהּ סְרִיקִין?
phrases.english: he would be liable even though the group is not entirely idlers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's statement using an inference from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's rule that he is liable only with a group made up entirely of idlers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only the מצוה as the reason for exemption, implying any non-מצוה group, even a decent one, makes him liable.

steps.title: Even idlers at a מצוה gathering do not pull him down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching a bigger point: even if the group is all idlers, the מצוה protects him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה teaches: even if the group is all idlers, since they are busy with a מצוה, he will not be pulled after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the משנה is really coming to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is a group of idlers who are doing a מצוה. Without the מצוה they would make him liable, as רבי אבהו said. The מצוה changes things, because people busy with a מצוה will not drag him into bad ways, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A בן סורר ומורה is liable only for eating with a group of all idlers, and even such a group does not make him liable if they are gathered for a מצוה.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that even though the group is entirely idlers,
since they are busy with a מצוה,
he will not be drawn after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by reinterpreting the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה's case so it fits רבי אבהו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies a non-מצוה group makes him liable even if it is not all idlers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a group of all idlers; the מצוה exempts him even then, so רבי אבהו stands.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Eating at the Month-Extension Meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: the son ate at the עיבור החודש meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he ate at the meal for adding a day to the month (he is not liable).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new case from the משנה. This is a setup line: the גמרא is about to ask a question on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the עיבור החודש meal as a case where the son is not liable. That is because he ate while busy with a מצוה. The גמרא now picks up these words so it can examine them.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding a day to the month (making it 30 days), decided by the חכמים

phrases.english: He ate at the intercalation of the month.
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה. They mean he ate at the gathering held to add a day to the month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general מצוה-group case to a specific example listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating meat and wine at the עיבור החודש meal does not make the son a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Were Meat and Wine Even Brought There?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the son could eat meat and wine there, since a ברייתא says only bread and legumes are brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean meat and wine are brought up there? But a ברייתא teaches: they go up for it only with bread of grain and legumes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's case. A ברייתא says the עיבור החודש meal only had bread and legumes, so where would meat and wine come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to assume that meat and wine were served at this meal. The ברייתא says the menu was only simple food. So the case in the משנה seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (opens a surprised question)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: Is this to say that meat and wine are brought up?
phrases.notes: "Brought up" because the חכמים went up to an upper room to decide on the month.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: they do not go up for it
except with bread of grain and legumes alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of eating meat and wine at the עיבור החודש meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says only bread and legumes are brought to that meal. So meat and wine would never be there, and the משנה's case could not happen.

steps.title: Even If He Brought Meat on His Own, the מצוה Protects Him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that even if the son brought up meat and wine himself, he is not liable because he is busy with a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה teaches us: even though they normally go up only with bread and legumes, if he brought up meat and wine and ate, he will not be drawn after it, since they are busy with a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה agrees meat and wine were not normally served. It is teaching about a son who brought them on his own, and even he is not liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not describing the usual menu. It describes an unusual son who brought meat and wine himself. Even so, the מצוה setting keeps him from being drawn into a bad path. This matches the idea from step 15 that the מצוה protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
He will not be drawn (after his appetite into a bad path)

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ
phrases.english: even though they do not go up for it
except with bread and legumes,
and he brought up meat and wine and ate,
since he is busy with a מצוה –
he will not be drawn.
phrases.notes: He means he won't be pulled into bad ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the son brought the meat and wine himself, which was not the normal menu.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to assume meat and wine were part of the regular meal, which would clash with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat and wine were not normally served. Even a son who brought them himself is not liable, because the מצוה setting protects him.

steps.title: The Rules for Going Up to Extend the Month
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists rules for the עיבור החודש gathering: at least ten men, only bread and legumes, only on its night, and at night rather than by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: no fewer than ten men go up for the עיבור החודש. They go up only with bread of grain and legumes. They go up only on the night of its extension. They do not go up by day, only at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a full ברייתא that lays out the rules for the עיבור החודש gathering. It includes the bread-and-legumes rule we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא gives four rules: a minimum of ten people, a simple menu, the right night, and nighttime rather than daytime. The last rule will be challenged right away in the next step.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
They do not go up for the intercalation of the month
with fewer than ten people,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ אֶלָּא בְּפַת דָּגָן וְקִטְנִית,
phrases.english: and they go up for it only with bread of grain and legumes,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ אֶלָּא לְאוֹר עִיבּוּרוֹ,
phrases.english: and they go up for it only on the night of its intercalation,
phrases.notes: Here "אור" means the night, not light. It is like "אור לארבעה עשר," the night of the fourteenth.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בַּיּוֹם אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: and they do not go up for it by day, only at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹלִין בְּעִיבּוּר הַחוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the full ברייתא whose bread-and-legumes rule was quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עיבור החודש gathering needs at least ten men, simple food only, and takes place on the night of the extension, at night rather than by day.

steps.title: A Contradiction: Night or Day?
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says they go up only by day, not at night, which contradicts the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: they do not go up for it at night, only by day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the exact opposite about the time of going up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said night, not day. This one says day, not night. Both cannot seem to be right.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: they do not go up for it at night
but only by day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last rule of the ברייתא in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that they go up at night and not by day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite times, night and day. So they directly contradict each other.

steps.title: Go Up Early and Leave Early
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from רבי חייא בר אבא's advice to his sons: go up early and leave early so people hear about it. The time is at the border of night and day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said to his sons: go up early and leave early, so that people will hear about you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction with a saying of רבי חייא בר אבא. He told his sons to go early and leave early so people would notice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going up very early means it is still dark, at the edge between night and day. One ברייתא calls that time "night" and the other calls it "day," so they do not really argue. People seeing them come and go would learn that the month was being dealt with.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַאֲמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said to his sons:
go up early, and go out early,
phrases.notes: Going up so early that it is still almost night is how both ברייתות can be right: it is the edge of night and day.

phrases.english: so that people will hear of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאֲמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonizing two sources: both describe the same early hour between night and day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite times, night versus day.
steps.terutzMaskana: They go up very early, at the edge of night and day. This time can be called either night or day, and going early lets people hear about the עיבור.
steps.whatToRemember: The עיבור החודש gathering: at least ten men, simple food only, and going up and leaving very early so people notice.

steps.title: Eating Second Tithe in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: If the son ate מעשר שני in ירושלים, he is not liable, because he is eating it the proper way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he ate מעשר שני in ירושלים. Since he is eating it the way it is meant to be eaten, he will not be drawn after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case from the משנה and explains why the son is not liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is meant to be eaten in ירושלים. A son eating it there is doing what the תורה wants. So this eating does not show a pull toward gluttony that would lead him astray.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that must be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: He ate second tithe in Jerusalem.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי אוֹרְחֵיהּ הוּא קָא אָכֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Since he is eating it in its normal way,
he will not be drawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next exemption in the משנה, using the same 'he will not be drawn' reasoning as step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating מעשר שני in ירושלים does not make the son a בן סורר ומורה, since it is eaten in its proper, מצוה way.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Forbidden Meats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a son who ate נבילות, טריפות, שקצים, and רמשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he ate נבילות and טריפות, שקצים and רמשים (he is not liable).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case from the משנה. This is a setup line for רבא's statement about what kind of meat counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that eating these forbidden meats does not make the son a בן סורר ומורה. Quoting this case opens the topic of which kinds of meat count, and רבא adds to it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that died without proper שחיטה
Animals with a fatal injury or defect

phrases.english: He ate unslaughtered carcasses and tereifot,
repugnant creatures and creeping animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next exemption listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating forbidden meats does not make the son a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: רבא: Fowl Meat Does Not Count
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the son ate bird meat, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he ate bird meat, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new ruling about which kind of meat counts: bird meat does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son becomes liable only for eating meat (and drinking wine). רבא teaches that bird meat does not fit this requirement, even though it is kosher. So eating it does not make him a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.confusionAlert: Bird meat is kosher and allowed! רבא is not calling it forbidden. He is only saying it does not count toward the meat needed to make a son a בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
if he ate the meat of fowl –
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's forbidden meats, רבא adds that even kosher bird meat does not count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating bird meat does not make the son a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: The משנה seems to say kosher meat, including bird meat, does make him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה says non-kosher meat does not make him a בן סורר ומורה, which implies kosher meat, including birds, does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: if he ate נבילות and טריפות, or שקצים and רמשים, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה? That implies that if he ate kosher meat, he does become a בן סורר ומורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling from Step 24 by reading the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only excludes non-kosher meat. So it seems any kosher meat counts, and kosher birds are kosher meat. That clashes with רבא, who said bird meat does not make him a בן סורר ומורה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? It opens a challenge from a משנה.
Meat of animals that died without proper שחיטה
Animals with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
If he ate נבילות and טריפות,
repugnant creatures and creeping animals,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.
This implies: if he ate kosher ones,
phrases.notes: Kosher meat includes kosher birds, and that is what makes this a problem for רבא.

phrases.english: he does become a stubborn and rebellious son?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that eating bird meat does not make him a בן סורר ומורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה excludes only non-kosher meat, which implies all kosher meat, birds included, makes him liable.

steps.title: Bird meat only helps complete the amount
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's implication about kosher meat refers to bird meat completing the required amount, not being the main meat he ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught this too, it meant to complete the amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps רבא's ruling standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird meat alone does not make him liable, which is רבא's point. But if he ate regular meat and added some bird meat to reach the full amount, it counts, and that is what the משנה implies. So the two sources talk about different situations.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean bird meat counts as the main meal. It only counts as an add-on to complete the amount.

phrases.english: When we learned it in the משנה as well,
it was to complete the amount.
phrases.notes: He means bird meat can help fill up the needed amount alongside regular meat, but cannot be the main meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: main eating vs. completing the amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies kosher bird meat fully makes him liable, against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bird meat alone does not make him liable (רבא); it only counts toward completing the amount (the משנה).
steps.whatToRemember: Bird meat alone does not make a בן סורר ומורה, but it can help complete the amount.

steps.title: Eating connected to a מצוה or to an עבירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about eating tied to a מצוה or an עבירה, and gives examples: comforting mourners and a public fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate something that is a מצוה, or something that is an עבירה, he is not liable. 'Something that is a מצוה' means comforting mourners. 'Something that is an עבירה' means a public fast day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and explains it with examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examples show the rule reaches even rabbinic cases. Eating at a meal for comforting mourners is a מצוה from the רבנן, and eating on a תענית ציבור breaks a rabbinic rule. Either way he is not a בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: If he ate something that is a מצוה,
or something that is a sin.
Something that is a מצוה: comforting mourners,
something that is a sin: a public fast day.
phrases.notes: He means eating on a public fast day, when he should be fasting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה וּדְבַר עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating tied to a מצוה (even rabbinic, like comforting mourners) or to an עבירה (even rabbinic, like a public fast) does not make him a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Why does a מצוה or an עבירה exempt him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule in Step 27.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind the rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה case makes sense, but why should eating in a sinful way get him off? The גמרא wants the source.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why eating tied to a מצוה or an עבירה does not make him a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: The פסוק: 'he does not listen to our voice'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of a son who disobeys his parents' voice, not one who disobeys הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He does not listen to our voice.' Our voice, meaning the parents, and not the voice of the מקום (God).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרשה is about rebelling against parents. If his eating is also a sin against God, it is no longer just disobeying 'our voice', so it falls outside this law.

keyTerms.meaning: A name for הקדוש ברוך הוא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the core of this law: rebellion against parents, not sinning in general.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"He does not listen to our voice"
our voice, and not the voice of God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'our voice', so the law covers rebelling against parents only, not against God.
steps.whatToRemember: בן סורר ומורה is about disobeying parents ('our voice'), not about disobeying God.

steps.title: The משנה: any food but not meat, any drink but not wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if he ate any food but not meat, or drank any drink but not wine, he is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate any food but did not eat meat, or drank any drink but did not drink wine, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only meat and wine make him a בן סורר ומורה. The extra words 'any food' and 'any drink' seem unneeded, and the next step explains what they add.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: If he ate any food but did not eat meat,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתָה כׇּל מַשְׁקֶה וְלֹא שָׁתָה יַיִן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: drank any drink but did not drink wine, and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only meat and wine make him a בן סורר ומורה; other foods and drinks do not.

steps.title: What 'any food' and 'any drink' come to include
steps.stepSummary: 'Any food' includes pressed figs from קעילה, and 'any drink' includes honey and milk. None of these make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he ate any food but not meat' comes to include pressed figs from קעילה. 'If he drank any drink but not wine' comes to include honey and milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each phrase of the משנה and explains what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think foods very close to meat and wine also count. Pressed figs from קעילה fill a person up like meat, and honey and milk can make a person a bit drunk. The extra words teach that even these do not make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressed figs from the town of קעילה, very filling like meat

steps.whatToRemember: Only real meat and real wine count. Even foods that feel like them (figs from קעילה, honey, milk) do not.

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר –
phrases.english: 'If he ate any food but did not eat meat':
this comes to include pressed figs from קעילה.
phrases.notes: These figs were as filling as meat, so you might have thought they count like meat.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתָה כׇּל מַשְׁקֶה וְלֹא שָׁתָה יַיִן –
phrases.english: 'If he drank any drink but did not drink wine':
this comes to include honey and milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the extra words in the משנה quoted in Step 30 add.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pressed figs from קעילה, honey and milk do not make him a בן סורר ומורה, even though they are like meat and wine.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a כהן who ate figs or drank honey or milk and entered the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא. It describes a כהן who ate pressed figs from קעילה, or drank honey or milk, and then entered the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If a כהן ate pressed figs from קעילה, or drank honey or milk, and then entered the מקדש...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a ברייתא as a source to show that these foods can make a person drunk. This line only sets up the case. The ruling of the ברייתא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 listed pressed figs, honey and milk as examples that do not make the בן סורר ומורה liable. The ברייתא treats these same foods as things that can affect a כהן who goes in to do the עבודה. That shows they have an intoxicating effect, which explains why the משנה bothered to mention them at all.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא). This introduces a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
The Temple, where the כהנים do the עבודה.
Entered. Here it means the כהן went into the מקדש to serve.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about the בן סורר ומורה at all. It is about a כהן serving in the מקדש. The גמרא borrows it only to show that these foods can intoxicate.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If he ate pressed figs from Ke'ila,
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is a כהן. The ברייתא is talking about someone who serves in the מקדש.

phrases.english: or drank honey or milk,
and then entered the Temple –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the assumption behind Step 31: that pressed figs, honey and milk are intoxicating foods.
steps.raayaObject: That pressed figs from קעילה, honey and milk have an intoxicating effect, which is why the משנה had to say they do not make him liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a כהן who ate or drank these and then entered the מקדש. Its ruling follows in the next lines.
